title: Rent & Shelter
headline_read: The rental market is balanced — rents are behaving.

indicators.title: CPI: Rent of Primary Residence
indicators.context: The rent component of the Consumer Price Index — what tenants actually pay. It moves slowly but relentlessly, and it is a third of core CPI.
indicators.read: Rent costs are roughly flat over the past year.

indicators.title: CPI: Owners' Equivalent Rent
indicators.context: What homeowners would pay to rent their own homes — the largest single component of the CPI, and the bridge between home prices and inflation.
indicators.read: Owners' equivalent rent is up 3% from a year ago, now 441.

indicators.title: Rental Vacancy Rate
indicators.context: The share of rental units sitting empty (quarterly). Low vacancy gives landlords pricing power; high vacancy hands it back to renters.
indicators.read: Rental vacancy is 7.3% — a healthy balance between renters and landlords.

indicators.title: Homeownership Rate
indicators.context: The share of households that own their home (quarterly) — the long arc of whether owning is gaining or losing ground versus renting.
indicators.read: The homeownership rate is 65.3%, up 0.2 points from a year ago.
